conventions.convention: Sources are jointly smooth conserved volume densities on R³ × R, supported in one fixed closed spatial ball at every time. Compact support in time is unnecessary. Singular sources and independently added homogeneous fields are excluded.

Radiation limits follow x = rn and t = u + r/c, keeping retarded time u fixed, uniformly in direction and on every compact retarded-time interval. Scaled electric and magnetic data have units V and T m.

The quantitative far-field bounds use r ≥ 2a, a nondegenerate compact interval K, and source derivative suprema on K enlarged by 2a/c at each endpoint. SI constants satisfy ε₀ = 1/(μ₀c²), and outward flux uses S = E × B/μ₀.
Taylor truncation order N is any integer ≥ 0. Error bounds are absolute, use derivatives through order N+2, and assert neither infinite-series convergence nor a relative estimate at dipole nodes.

Countable Choice is assumed for the measure, change-of-variables, surface-integration and Banach-valued Taylor suppliers. All physical conclusions are conditional model deductions, without empirical claims.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice; a,c,μ₀ > 0; ε₀ = 1/(μ₀c²); and jointly smooth conserved ρ,J on R³ × R vanishing whenever |y| > a. The displayed retarded potential integrals converge absolutely everywhere, are jointly smooth, satisfy Wφ = ρ/ε₀, WA = μ₀J and Lorenz gauge, and generate smooth Maxwell fields everywhere on the adopted retarded branch without an independent homogeneous addition. No compact support in time is assumed.

Under its Countable Choice, smooth conserved fixed-ball source and SI retarded-field hypotheses, for every n ∈ S², u ∈ K and r ≥ 2a, the electric leading field μ₀ n × (n × V(n,u))/(4πr) has error at most Γ_E/r² and its associated magnetic leading field has error at most Γ_B/r². The resulting radiation data exist uniformly on S² × K. At each fixed u the outward flux limit is μ₀/(16π²c) times the sphere integral of |n × V(n,u)|².

Assume Countable Choice and the source, SI and retarded-field hypotheses of the preceding transverse-radiation theorem on a nondegenerate compact interval K. For every integer N ≥ 0, the displayed finite coefficient has |V − J_N| ≤ R_N, the stated electric-field bound and the stated absolute integrated-power bound. For N = 0, J_0 = p'' and |P − μ₀|p''|²/(6πc)| ≤ μ₀(2|p''|R_0 + R_0²)/(4πc). No infinite Taylor convergence or relative error at an angular node is asserted.
